evidence: Liu2025ElasticMM PDF Sec 3.1 (Proactive Mechanism, p.5): idle elastic instances are proactively assigned by a greedy max-min burst-tolerance heuristic, bt(i)=N_peak_i/N_avg_i (Eq.1), computed over long-term AGGREGATE load statistics -- exactly 'static allocation of idle instances by a long-run burst-tolerance heuristic over aggregate load'. No forecasting model exists (thresholds from offline profiling; day/night periodicity of aggregate load is assumed, not predicted), confirming 'not a per-pool demand forecast'. The paper's own words (Sec 3.1, p.5): 'the short-term arrival pattern of a single request stream is difficult to predict' -- the parenthetical the thesis quotes is verbatim. ElasticMM also has a reactive scaling/gain-cost mechanism, but the thesis's 'predominantly reactive' framing already accounts for that and attributes only the static idle allocation to ElasticMM's proactive addition, so the claim is accurate.
